repo.description:
---
  Impact

  Vulnerability Type: Open Redirect

  Description:
  The enter action in StaticController reads the sso_destination_url cookie and redirects to it with allow_other_host:
  true without validating the destination URL. While this cookie is normally set during legitimate DiscourseConnect
  Provider flows with cryptographically validated SSO payloads, cookies are client-controlled and can be set by
  attackers.

  Attack Scenario:
  An attacker who can set cookies in a victim's browser (via subdomain cookie injection, XSS on a related domain, or
  other cookie-setting vulnerabilities) can set the sso_destination_url cookie to an arbitrary external URL (e.g.,
  https://evil-phishing-site.com/login). When the victim authenticates via POST to /login, they are redirected to the
  attacker-controlled URL, enabling phishing attacks.

  Who is Impacted:
  - Sites using DiscourseConnect Provider (enable_discourse_connect_provider = true)
  - Users authenticating via the /login endpoint when an attacker can set cookies in their browser

  Severity: High - Enables phishing attacks post-authentication

  ---
  Patches

  The vulnerability has been patched by adding validation to ensure the sso_destination_url cookie value matches
  configured SSO provider domains before allowing external redirects.

  What Changed:
  - The enter action now validates the cookie value against the discourse_connect_provider_secrets site setting
  - Only URLs matching configured provider domains (including wildcard domains) are allowed for external redirects
  - Invalid or unauthorized URLs fall back to safe internal redirects

  Recommended Action:
  Users should upgrade to the latest stable version that includes this security fix.

  ---
  Workarounds

  If immediate upgrade is not possible, consider these temporary mitigations:

  1. Disable DiscourseConnect Provider (if not actively used). `enable_discourse_connect_provider = false`. This prevents the vulnerable code path from being executed.

  Note: These are temporary mitigations only. Upgrading is strongly recommended.
  ---
  References

  - https://meta.discourse.org/t/using-discourse-as-a-sso-provider/32974
